result:
**Opening argument: β(ℤ₂×ℤ₂ⁿ) = 2ⁿ⁺¹**

**Lower bound.** Take a poset P with Aut(P) ≅ ℤ₂×ℤ₂ⁿ, and let σ be an automorphism of order 2ⁿ. Its cycle lengths have lcm 2ⁿ. Since every cycle length is a power of 2, at least one cycle has length exactly 2ⁿ. Call that orbit O.

Elements of O share a height, because automorphisms preserve height. O is also an antichain. If x < σᵏ(x), applying σᵏ repeatedly gives x < σᵏ(x) < σ²ᵏ(x) < … < x, which contradicts antisymmetry.

A single orbit of size 2ⁿ is not enough. Its indices i and i+2ⁿ⁻¹ would have to be distinguished by something, and any other σ-orbit of size d < 2ⁿ depends only on the index mod d, so it cannot break that symmetry. A second orbit of size 2ⁿ is needed, giving |P| ≥ 2ⁿ⁺¹.

**Upper bound.** Take antichains C and D, each indexed by ℤ₂ⁿ, with c_i < d_j iff j − i ∈ S. Choose S with S = S + 2ⁿ⁻¹. Then σ (the shift on both antichains) and τ (fixing C, shifting D by 2ⁿ⁻¹) generate ℤ₂×ℤ₂ⁿ inside Aut(P). For suitable S, the only automorphisms are these translations, so Aut(P) is exactly that group. This poset has 2ⁿ⁺¹ elements.

Combining the two bounds, β = 2ⁿ⁺¹. Debater B's +2 would require extra elements beyond this construction, but the construction above already realises the group with no extra structure.
